items.text: Sam 'said he'd look into the flaky CI before Friday': Due is 'none' (could be 2026-10-08). C6, reviewer A1: 'whether the notes make the date clear is for the lead'.
Marta 'book the on-call training room for Oct 14': Due is 'none', Oct 14 kept in the Action cell (could be Due 2026-10-14). C6, reviewer A2: 'reads as the training date, not a booking deadline'.
The 'Present' line and 'Next meeting' line are in the memo; they are not decisions or action items. C2/C3, reviewer A3: 'lead decides whether to keep'.

Marta row / Open questions, C3 and C6: the notes say the room is booked "for Oct 14" and do not literally say the training is on Oct 14. Reviewer: "natural but not literal reading"; a stricter reader could want "room needed for Oct 14". No Due value changes (Marta stays none).

Open questions section, C3: reviewer: a strict reading of "no statement that is not in the file" could apply beyond the Decisions section. Every statement there is derived from the notes (Friday of that week = 2026-10-09 follows from "Monday 5 October 2026").

C6, Marta's Due: 'Oct 14' is the training date, not stated as a booking deadline (reviewer: "Marta's 'Oct 14' is the training date and not stated as a booking deadline"). Memo uses 2026-10-14 per your ruling.
C6, Sam's Due: 'before Friday' could mean Thursday (reviewer: "Sam's 'before Friday' could mean Thursday"). Memo uses 2026-10-09 per your ruling.
C3, Lee's item: whether 'we agreed' is a decision (reviewer's words). It is a table row, not in Decisions.

Sam staging row (C5/C6): hedged 'will probably sort it out himself'; included as a row, Due 2026-10-21 (day before the Oct 22 freeze). Reviewer: 'If the reader thinks the hedge makes the date unclear, none would be the alternative.'
Lee shift swap row (C6): 'demo week' gives no date, Due none.
Sam CI update and 'Nobody had a problem with that' (C3/C5): reviewer did not count them as decision or action item; not in memo.
Present / Next meeting lines (C2/scope): reviewer says they could be dropped if scope is strictly decisions + actions (accepted in the 10-05 memo).
C7 (reviewer: 'circular, concerns this report and applied changes'): reviewer counted C7 outside its 9 of 9; no changes were required, so none were left unapplied.
C3/C5 Sam's row (reviewer: "hedge 'will probably'"): row kept with Due 2026-10-21 per your ruling.
C3/C5 Lee's shift swap (reviewer: 'could also count as a decision; memo lists it as an action only').
C7 (circular, reviewer: 'C7 ambiguous (circular). It depends on this report'): reviewer found no required changes, so nothing was left unapplied.

C10 scope (reviewer: 'Lee Action cell still names Dev ... C10 and R3 are about the Owner column only'): kept as is, per your note that names may stay in Action text. Say if you want initials there too.
C6, rows 2 and 6: Due 'none' for 'probably by end of next week' (Lee) and 'during that first week' (Sam). Reviewer: 'kept as none; settled rule from earlier runs'.
C3: Summary says 'took six action items'; the notes give no count, it equals the six table rows. Reviewer: 'listed for you to decide'.
C5: row 6 treats 'Sam offered to pair with Jo' as a commitment (reviewer: informal, settled in earlier reviews).
C10: Action cells name people ('Lee:', 'Jo') outside the Owner column. Reviewer: 'not a C10 failure'.
C5 (every commitment is a row): Marta's 'keep the agenda as sent' is no longer a row, per your ruling 3. Reviewer A1: 'If C5 is read literally, it conflicts with the ruling.'
C6: Lee's Due 2026-10-30 is not in the notes ('probably by end of next week'). Reviewer A2: 'by C6 alone it would be none'; the hedge no longer shows in the memo.
Summary 'five action items': reviewer A3: count not stated in notes, derived; equals the 5 table rows.

Summary line says "took five action items", a count not stated in the notes (derived; reviewer's own count is also 5). C3/C9, reviewer: "Summary clause 'took five action items' is a derived count... no change required." Is a derived count acceptable in the Summary?

Summary says 'took five action items': a count derived from the notes, not stated in them (C3 'no statement not in the file' / C9 'summarizes the meeting'). Reviewer: "a count not stated in the notes (derived; my count is also 5). Not required to change." Kept as verified.

Lee 'check the SSO renewal invoice ... on Wednesday', Due 'none' (C6): reviewer: 'a future Wednesday would be 2026-11-04, but the notes also use Wednesday for the past cutover, so none is defensible; client could rule otherwise.' Should it be 2026-11-04?
JD owner (C11): kept as written in the notes ('JD'); reviewer: fine under C11 as worded.

Sam's bare 'by Friday' (C6): the memo uses 2026-11-13 (Friday after the Monday 9 Nov meeting). Reviewer: "Sam's 'by Friday' read as 2026-11-13 per the settled rule... the lead decides if the client rules otherwise." Does a bare weekday count as a clear date, or should Due be 'none'?
